Whether or not a game is worth the price tag, for me, comes down to my level of enthusiasm for the title.

My enthusiasm can change based on many factors, including prior exposure to a title (have I played its sequels, or is it a new release), whether or not it is part of an established series I regularly play, and if the series has failed to meet my expectations previously.

Action adventure games like Far Cry 4 or Tomb Raider will get a full price buy (60 + tax) if they are open world, there is no agenda present and of course are AAA titles.

Survival horror games I will wait for reviews and most of the time I will wait for a sale. Shooters are my least favorite, things like Halo or Call of Duty. A usual decision tool I use, is will I get an hour of playtime per dollar I spend? Five dollar game, will I get five hours of time and enjoyment? Sixty dollar game will I get sixty hours of enjoyment?

However, over time and depending on the circumstances, this has changed to will I get more enjoyment from this game than spending the equivalent on other entertainment? So if the game is ten bucks, would I rather watch a two hour movie that cost ten dollars or buy this game?

Overall though, my best tool is will I actually play this? Not a genre I enjoy playing buy like watching? Then I can watch it on twitch and save the money. A genre I love, play heavily, has good reviews, storytelling, modern graphics, etc.? I'll probably get it on a steam sale at least.
